topic: Maki's grade 4 rank was held down by her clan, per chapter 40
title: Maki Zenin Was Held At Grade 4 On Purpose
description: Gojo and Mei Mei both say Maki should be at least grade 2 in chapter 40. Here is why she wasn't, and what it says about her clan. Was the rank a mistake or a punishment?
comment: Was the Zenin clan right to fear Maki, or did they just hate being wrong? Pick one.
end_text: WHERE HER POWER REALLY CAME FROM

lines.text: Maki Zenin was never really grade 4, and her teachers knew it.

shot.fallback: student looking at a ranking board

lines.text: Chapter 40 is where two sorcerers say it out loud.

shot.fallback: white haired teacher beside a woman in a crow themed jacket

lines.text: Gojo and Mei Mei agree she should be grade 2 at least.
She can handle a grade 2 curse with ease, so the number made no sense.

shot.fallback: woman swinging a spear at a monster

lines.text: The reason is the clan. Tension with the Zenin family stalled her promotion.

shot.fallback: stern elders in a traditional hall

lines.text: Same chapter, the Goodwill Event. She beats Kasumi Miwa, a sword user, with plain aikido.
So the skeptic says rank reflects power, and a girl without cursed energy deserves grade 4.
Except rank is about what you can exorcise, and she was already doing grade 2 work.
The clan didn't misjudge her. It kept the number low because a low number kept her small.

shot.fallback: girl walking away from an estate gate

lines.text: She had the skill long before any twin's gift. So what did that gift change?
Because the rank was a lie, and Maki Zenin was never really grade 4.

self_check.hook: Opens with a contrarian claim about her rank.
self_check.loop: Last line leads back into line 1.
